For the children. For the curious.

Everyday Cool Arcade

Every game in the Everyday Cool collection, gathered on one shelf — and every game keeps its back door attached. Play first. Then open the lesson: the physics, the math, and how the game itself is built, in plain language. That is what makes an arcade a teacher can say yes to.

37 games · 36 with lessons attached

Finding your way back: from any game, use the browser-style back gesture — Alt + ← or your mouse's back button — to return to this shelf. Lessons opened from a card read right here; several games also carry a 📖 Lesson button inside the game itself.

📦 The Baton Box — the family post office

The Baton Box is a small server that runs on this computer. It serves the DOS Console with the cross-origin isolation headers it needs, and it relays the pass-and-play games — The Relay, the 6502 Bench, the NES, SNES, and DOS consoles — to everyone on your home network: a phone, a tablet, the kids' iPads, anything on the same Wi-Fi as this machine.

Start it here, then open the box in your browser to host or join a game. Stop puts it away. It runs with this computer's Python — the same Python the standalone Baton Box uses — and it only ever serves your home network.
